name: Typewriter dialogue box
oneLiner: Story text in a framed box at the bottom (or top) of the screen: each line types out letter by letter with small pauses at punctuation, a name tag sits on the speaker's side, a blinking arrow waits for Z / Enter / tap, which first finishes the page and then advances; holding fast-forwards. Long lines wrap and page at native resolution, the box moves to the top when the speaker stands under it and never covers the HUD. Lines are a plain array of {speaker, text} the designer edits; the world pauses while it is open and the game gets onEnd back.
fits: top-down adventure and RPG (talking to people, signs, chests)
turn-based RPG battle (intro and victory lines, boss taunts)
side-scrolling platformer or action game (story beats between stages)
visual-novel style scenes inside a game
notFor: speech bubbles that float over moving characters while play continues (a different element)
full visual novels with portraits, backlog and save per line (portraits are family D)
branching choices and story flags (H-02 builds on this element's line format)
subtitles for voiced dialogue timed to audio

needs: the game's existing function that shows text (talking, signs, item messages), in update logic: open(lines, {onEnd}) there; what ran after the old text closed moves into onEnd
the confirm input routed to the box while busy() (press() on the key-down edge, optional hold(down), or key(code, down))
a fixed 60 Hz update step (the box's only clock), also while the world is paused for the box
the play field size in native px
optional: the speaker's sprite rect on screen (getAnchor(who, line)) and ui rects to keep clear (HUD, menus)
provides: busy flag: route the confirm input here and pause the world while the box is open
conversation end via onEnd({lines, index, skipped, auto, line}) (synchronous, inside update())
per-line hooks onLine / onLineEnd (return false to hold the box on a line: choices, pop-ups) and next / goto / insert / end
a per-letter sound hook (onTick) for the game's text blip, and sound cue names (onSfx)
the box rectangle on screen (incl. the name tag), for other overlays to avoid
the H-01 dialogue box itself (open / busy / rect, lines with who and expr) that expressive portraits (D-04) and dialogue choices (H-02) attach to

params.label: Which text goes in the box (required; the designer's words)
params.default: everything the game already shows as text in a message box: talking to characters, reading signs, item and chest messages

params.label: Letters per second (0 = whole page at once)
Auto-advance (ms after a page is complete; 0 = wait for the player)
Window colour (a blue, n slate, b red)

assets: module/dialogue-box.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_DialogueBox): script parsing, word wrap and paging, typewriter with punctuation pauses, name tag, more arrow, input (press / hold / key), placement, autoplay, drawing with the C-03 6x8 font built in
no image or audio files (the letter tick is a callback; the game plays its own sound)
